h1: Amber Sands Beach Resort — a small resort with a private beach on the quiet side of Koh Chang
intro: Picture this: you wake up, open your bungalow door, and there's a quiet stretch of sand with clear sea right in front of you — no music from a bar, no crowds of tourists, just the soft sound of the waves. Amber Sands Beach Resort is a small family-run resort on the east coast of Koh Chang, in the Salak Phet Bay–Dan Kao area, the side everyone knows as the "quiet and peaceful" one, the opposite of the lively White Sand Beach · What real reviews talk about most is the private beach with almost no one else on it, owners who look after you like family, and genuinely good food · There are just 8 beachfront bungalows, from around THB 2,500/night · It sits at #1 of 139 B&Bs on Koh Chang on TripAdvisor with 4.9/5 from 697 reviews, and 9.6 on Trip.com.

body.html: Who Amber Sands is for — the shortest way to put it: Amber Sands Beach Resort is for people who come to Koh Chang to actually "rest," not to party · It's not a big resort with multi-tier infinity pools or a ten-metre breakfast buffet, and it's not a place on White Sand Beach where you step out the door into rows of restaurants and bars · Instead it's a tiny resort with just 8 bungalows, run by the owner's family who look after guests themselves every day, set on a private beach on the northeastern side of the island in the Salak Phet Bay–Dan Kao area, the quietest, most peaceful part of Koh Chang · Real reviews on TripAdvisor, Booking.com and Trip.com all point the same way: the people who suit this place are couples after a quiet, romantic feel, families bringing small children to swim at a safe beach, and travellers who want to escape the chaos and just be with nature and the sea at an unhurried pace · On the flip side, anyone chasing nightlife, a range of restaurants within walking distance, or five-star luxury might find it too quiet · Plenty of reviews use words like "tucked away" and "like finding a little treasure" to describe that first impression, because it's a place that doesn't advertise loudly — but people who've stayed once tend to come back, which is the best sign you can get from a small resort like this.

Location and getting there — this is the thing to understand clearly before you book, because Amber Sands' location is both its selling point and the part you have to plan around · The resort is on the northeastern side of Koh Chang, in the Baan Dan Kao area near Salak Phet Bay, a side most tourists don't really go to, since the popular beaches — White Sand Beach, Klong Prao and Kai Bae — are all on the west coast · The upside is that this side is quiet and peaceful, with calm, shallow water and almost no one else on the beach, which suits families and anyone who wants privacy · The thing to note is that there are barely any restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance of the resort — several reviews from overseas guests say the same thing: "there's nowhere to walk to except the resort next door," so if you want to eat out or visit other beaches, you'll need to rent a motorbike or arrange a ride · Getting to the island: drive or take a transfer to the car ferry pier (Centerpoint or Ao Thammachat) at Laem Ngop in Trat province, then take the ferry across to Koh Chang, roughly 30–45 min · From the Salak Phet pier on the island it's only a few kilometres to the resort, much closer than heading over to the west coast · The resort offers a pier transfer, so let them know your arrival time in advance to keep it easy · If you fly into Trat Airport (TDX) and then take a transfer to the pier, that's another option, and a faster one than driving from Bangkok all day.

"You open your room door and there's the private beach right there. All day you barely see anyone except the handful of other guests · The owner and his family look after you like an old friend, and the food is delicious every meal — this is the Koh Chang we came looking for."

Room types and decor — Amber Sands has just 8 bungalows, which keeps the feel friendly and uncrowded · From the reviews and booking info, the rooms come in a few types, starting with the Superior Bungalow, the entry-level room with a Queen bed · Stepping up are the Beachfront Bungalows, both downstairs and upstairs, set right by the sea with a full beach view, plus a 2-Bedroom Bungalow with one Queen and two single beds for families · What reviews consistently praise is that the rooms are spacious, clean and genuinely right on the sea — many say you open the door and you're a few steps from the sand · The decor is simple but warm seaside-resort style, leaning on wood tones and natural colours, not flashy but well kept · Every room has air conditioning, a private balcony or porch for sitting and looking at the sea, a fridge and an en-suite bathroom · The beds get praise for being soft and comfortable, and many reviews mention falling asleep to the sound of the waves as an experience you can't get at a big resort · Because it's a small place the owners run themselves, cleanliness and upkeep stay consistent, and that's something reviews score highly again and again · One thing to know is that the beachfront rooms are limited and the most in demand, so if you want one, book well ahead.

Facilities, pool and activities — for a small resort, Amber Sands has a surprisingly complete set of facilities for a beach holiday · The highlight is the outdoor sea-view pool set between the bungalows and the beach, looking out over the wide bay, a spot guests love to settle into in the afternoon and evening · There's a separate kids' pool, so families with little ones can relax · What impresses a lot of reviewers is the free kayaks, paddle boats and paddleboards, because the sea on this side is calm and shallow, perfect for paddling around the bay · On top of that there are free bicycles, beachside massage, umbrellas and sun loungers on the beach, free parking and free Wi-Fi · They can arrange snorkelling, diving and boat trips for anyone who wants to head out and explore the nearby islands · To be straight with you, the beach on this side isn't the fine white sand of the west coast — it's a quiet beach that, in places, has natural sediment mixed into the sand, as the east coast tends to · But for privacy and peace, it gives you something that's hard to find on Koh Chang these days · Another thing reviews mention often is the daily beachside happy hour, which has become a favourite time for guests to sit, watch the sun and chat.

Food and bar — this is another strength that comes up most in real reviews of Amber Sands · The resort has a beachfront restaurant and bar serving both Thai and Western food · A lot of guests agree the food is better than you'd expect from a resort this small, especially breakfast and dinner, which many say are good enough that you don't want to go out to eat — which works out well, since there's barely anywhere else around anyway · The menu adapts to fresh ingredients and what guests want, and the owner and family listen and make things the way you ask · The beachfront bar has drinks and cocktails, plus that happy hour that becomes a routine for many guests · Dining here is laid-back, feet in the sand, listening to the waves, watching the sun drop below the horizon · Because it's on the east coast, sunrise is especially lovely in the morning, while the evening still gets soft light over the bay · The one limitation worth knowing is that the menu isn't as varied as restaurants in town or on the White Sand Beach side, since it's the resort's small kitchen — but what they do make earns steady praise for taste and care · If you're worried about food options, it's worth renting a motorbike for the days you fancy a change of scene and want to try somewhere else on the island.

Service — if there's one thing that keeps Amber Sands at #1 of 139 B&Bs on Koh Chang, it's the service · Because it's a family-run resort, the owner (reviews mention him by name, Simon) and his family look after guests themselves every day — from the welcome, to tips on where to go, to arranging boat trips, to cooking · Many reviews use phrases like "it feels like staying at a friend's house" and "more care than the price suggests" · A lot of people mention the owner remembering their names, remembering their favourite drinks, and checking in to ask what they feel like doing that day · That level of attention is something big resorts can't give, and it's the main reason many guests come back or recommend the place · One small thing that comes with being a small place: the team is limited, so at busy times or when the owner is away, service can slow a little, and there's no big-hotel setup like 24-hour room service or an all-night front desk · But overall, service is the heart of this place and its clearest strength.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulled together from TripAdvisor, Booking.com and Trip.com, the picture is strikingly consistent · On the praise side: a quiet private beach with almost no one else on it, an owner and family who look after you warmly like relatives, good food especially at breakfast and dinner, spacious clean rooms by the sea, the sea-view pool, free kayaks and paddle boats, and good value for what you get · Many reviews use "perfect stay" and "the best little hotel in Koh Chang" · On the notes side: the thing mentioned most is the quiet and the remoteness — the east coast has no restaurants, convenience stores or nightlife within walking distance, so anyone who wants buzz will find it too quiet and has to rely on a vehicle the whole time · Next is that the beach on this side isn't the fine white sand of the west coast — at low tide in places you'll see muddy ground mixed with sand, and some seasons bring sediment · On top of that, being a small place it has limited rooms, the beachfront rooms fill fast, and the facilities aren't as complete as a big resort's · Almost all of these notes are a matter of "is it your style" rather than actual faults — people who come because they want peace tend to see these as upsides.

"The best little resort I've stayed at on Koh Chang · quiet, peaceful, lovely owner, great food · The one thing to know is that it really is quiet — if you want lots of bars and restaurants, this isn't it — but for us it was paradise."

Price and value — Amber Sands' starting price is around THB 2,500/night for a Superior room in regular periods, climbing to roughly THB 3,500–5,500+ for a beachfront room or the two-bedroom bungalow in high season and on long weekends · Compared with the typical beachfront resort on Koh Chang, that's very good value once you count the privacy of the beach, the good food and the family-level care · What makes it especially worthwhile is the free extras like kayaks, paddle boats, bicycles and Wi-Fi, which many places on the island charge for · Compared with a big resort on the White Sand Beach side at a similar price, you'd get more luxury and more facilities, but in exchange for the chaos and the density of tourists · Whereas Amber Sands is selling peace, privacy and attentive service of a kind that's hard to buy at a chain resort · For people who weigh atmosphere and genuine rest over having every facility on tap, every baht you spend here pays you back in full.

Good to know before you book — a few things will make your stay smoother · One, rent a motorbike or have a transport plan ready, because there are no restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance of the resort — if you want to visit other beaches or change up where you eat, you'll need wheels · Two, book a beachfront room well ahead, since they're limited and the most in demand · Three, let the resort know your pier arrival time in advance so they can sort the transfer, and allow time for the ferry schedule at Laem Ngop · Four, check the seasonal opening and closing, because many small resorts on Koh Chang adjust their opening times around the monsoon — in low season (May–October) there's heavy rain and rougher seas, so ask before you book · Five, set your expectations right — you come here for peace and nature, not buzz or luxury; understand that from the start and you'll enjoy the stay a lot · Six, if you're travelling over a long weekend, compare prices across a few platforms and pick a free-cancellation option in case your plans change.

The verdict — from everything real reviews say, Amber Sands Beach Resort is the best fit for people who come to Koh Chang for peace, privacy and an unhurried seaside feel, at a price you can reach · A private beach with almost no one else on it, an owner and family who genuinely look after you, good food, and free extras like kayaks and paddle boats make it worthwhile enough to hold the #1 spot among B&Bs on Koh Chang for a long time · If you're after nightlife, a range of restaurants within walking distance, or a luxury resort with every facility covered, this might not be the answer, and you should look at resorts on the White Sand Beach or Klong Prao side instead · But for a trip where you want to escape the chaos and be with the quiet sea, in a place that looks after you like family — Amber Sands answers that need just about perfectly, and it's why people who've been tend to say the same thing: they want to come back.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Amber Sands Beach Resort, Koh Chang

faq.q: Where on Koh Chang is Amber Sands Beach Resort, and how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort is on the northeastern side of Koh Chang, in the Baan Dan Kao area near Salak Phet Bay, the quietest part of the island · You get there by taking the ferry across from Laem Ngop pier in Trat province, roughly 30–45 min, after which the Salak Phet pier is closest to the resort · The resort offers a pier transfer, so let them know your arrival time in advance.

It's a great fit for couples after a quiet, romantic feel, families bringing small children to swim at a safe beach, and people who want to escape the chaos and rest by the sea at an unhurried pace · If you're after nightlife, a range of restaurants within walking distance, or a luxury resort with every facility covered, the White Sand Beach or Klong Prao side might suit you better.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Amber Sands, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 2,500/night for a Superior Bungalow in regular periods · There are Beachfront Bungalows both downstairs and upstairs right by the sea, and a 2-Bedroom Bungalow for families · High-season and long-weekend prices climb to roughly THB 3,500–5,500+, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Are there restaurants or convenience stores around Amber Sands?
faq.a: Because it's on the quiet east coast, there are barely any restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance of the resort · But the resort has a beachfront restaurant and bar that earns praise for its food, especially breakfast and dinner · If you want to visit other beaches or change up where you eat, it's worth renting a motorbike.

faq.q: What pool and activities does Amber Sands have?
faq.a: There's an outdoor sea-view pool and a separate kids' pool, great for families · What impresses many reviewers is the free kayaks, paddle boats, paddleboards and bicycles, since the sea on this side is calm and shallow, perfect for paddling · There's beachside massage, umbrellas and sun loungers on the beach, and they can arrange snorkelling or boat trips for anyone who wants to head out and explore.

faq.q: Is Amber Sands actually good — what are the reviews like?
faq.a: Amber Sands holds #1 of 139 B&B/guesthouses on Koh Chang on TripAdvisor with 4.9/5 from 697 reviews, and 9.6 on Trip.com · Real reviews agree on the quiet private beach, the warm care from the owner and family, and the good food · The main note is the quiet and remoteness of the east coast, which people who come for peace tend to see as an upside.
